v.rationale: All three suites pass (11 tests each), and all three meet the core requirements: a nullable last_login_at column with a datetime cast, a #[Scope] that groups whereNull/orWhere correctly, --days defaulting to 90, a schedule entry at 06:00 that appends output to a log file, and RefreshDatabase enabled. I probed each one with --days=0, an empty value, a very large value, '+5', ' 5', '05' and CarbonImmutable dates. All three handle these consistently, except impl-1, whose scope throws a TypeError under CarbonImmutable because it type-hints a concrete Carbon class. impl-2 ranks first: the most rigorous tests (time frozen everywhere, exact output, boundary case, invalid-input dataset), tight code and an indexed column. Its only excess is withoutOverlapping, which a single server doesn't need. impl-1 ranks second: modern touches (the class reference in Schedule::command, $this->fail, a min_range check in one expression, a test that asserts the log path), offset by the latent Carbon type-hint bug, a factory state that adds ceremony and loose output assertions. impl-3 ranks third: correct and reasonably well tested, but it uses a heavyweight Validator for one integer, prints '1 users', leaves a stale commented line in Pest.php, has unsorted imports, makes a weak invalid-input assertion and has no boundary test.
